text:
emma-docs: Quick note — spotted an inconsistency in the /generate API page: examples still show `max_tokens` for streaming. Runtime expects `max_new_tokens` for incremental output. Can we update text + samples?

sanjay-eng: Yep that slipped through during the seq-length refactor. Behavior today: `max_tokens` is treated only for full (sync) completions; streaming uses `max_new_tokens`. We should mark `max_tokens` as deprecated for stream and add a migration blurb.

mike-ml: Also add the server-side precedence: if both `max_tokens` and `max_new_tokens` are present, `max_new_tokens` takes precedence. For function-calling flows call that out too.

emma-docs: Draft wording: "Use `max_new_tokens` to limit tokens emitted after the input when streaming. `max_tokens` is deprecated for streaming and will be ignored in streaming requests when `max_new_tokens` is provided." Any tweaks?

chris-pm: Sounds good. Avoid saying "ignored" maybe "not used". Also add a short migration example showing how to convert an existing request.

olivia-sdk: Heads up — our Python/Node helper layers still accept `max_tokens`. I can push a tiny compatibility change: if `max_new_tokens` missing and `max_tokens` present, map it internally and emit one deprecation log per process. Will also update README snippets.

emma-docs: Thanks. I'll change the curl examples. New SSE curl draft I'm thinking of including: ```bash
curl -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-stream","input":"Write a short summary","max_new_tokens":200,"stream":true}'
```

sanjay-eng: @olivia when you add the compatibility mapping, can you also have the SDK emit a visible deprecation warning in logs so integrators see it?

olivia-sdk: Yup. One-time warning per process. Also will update streaming examples in the SDK docs to use `max_new_tokens`.

mike-ml: Another small thing: the streaming message shape in the examples is inconsistent — some doc snippets use `remaining_tokens`, others `tokens_left`. We should standardize on `tokens_remaining` and make sure examples + SDK parsers accept the old keys for a transition window.

emma-docs: I'll standardize examples to `tokens_remaining` and add a footnote explaining the older names may be seen during the rollout.

ops-bot: Deploy started: runtime/streaming-schema-normalize (rolling) — approx 10m.

olivia-sdk: I'll add tolerant parsing for the response envelope: accept `tokens_left` or `remaining_tokens` and normalize to `tokens_remaining` in SDK outputs, warn in debug logs if legacy key seen.

chris-pm: Can we also add an entry to the top-level migration guide under "Request/param changes" with a tiny JS + Python before/after conversion? That helps support.

emma-docs: Will add a short migration note and link the generate page. Draft Python snippet for streaming example: ```py
# Python SDK streaming example
stream = client.generate_stream(model='redwood-1-stream', input='Summarize', max_new_tokens=120, stream=True)
for chunk in stream:
    print(chunk.text, end='')
```

sanjay-eng: Also make explicit: `max_new_tokens` caps the model-generated tokens only; when using function-calling the returned function args and the prompt both count toward the overall token budget, but the parameter limits the generation portion.
\em ma-docs: (typo) fixed — I'll add that note.

emma-docs: Checklist before PR: update generate ref schema text, replace curl/JS/Python examples, add migration bullet in migration guide, add precedence note for param conflicts, standardize response field to `tokens_remaining`. Tagging @olivia-sdk @sanjay-eng @mike-ml for review when I open the PR.

olivia-sdk: Ping when PR is up, will ready a small SDK patch in the same release window.

sanjay-eng: Thanks — will watch the runtime deploy and give a green when schema change is live.

ops-bot: Deploy complete: runtime/streaming-schema-normalize — success.
\em ma-docs: PR opened: docs: generate - prefer max_new_tokens for streaming + response field normalization. PTAL @olivia-sdk @sanjay-eng. :rocket:
